issues.description: Method Farm.addAnimal(Animal): The UML in problem_statement.md declares addAnimal(animal: Animal):boolean, but the solution implementation defines public void addAnimal(Animal animal) and the template Farm.java does not provide a completed addAnimal signature (only TODO scaffolding). This mismatch leaves students uncertain whether they should implement addAnimal to return a boolean (e.g., success flag) or to be void, and may cause compilation/test expectation differences.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the return type consistent. Preferred fixes (choose one to keep educational intent):
1) Update problem_statement.md UML to declare addAnimal(animal: Animal):void and update any task text that references the signature. This aligns with the solution implementation and keeps addAnimal as a simple mutator.
OR
2) Change the solution (and template scaffolding) to implement public boolean addAnimal(Animal animal) (returning true after successful add), and update the task text to instruct students to return a boolean. Ensure template method signature matches and tests (if any) expect boolean.
